free_tier.stated: "Consumption plan pricing includes a monthly free grant of 1 million requests and 400,000 GB-s of resource consumption per month per subscription in pay-as-you-go pricing across all function apps in that subscription." Footnote on the same page: "Free grants apply to the on-demand meters on paid, consumption subscriptions only."

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: 3,200,000 instance-seconds is the largest perpetual serverless budget found and it needs no IPv4 front, so it composes with an IPv6-only VPS as the scheduler that renews and health-checks it, or as the worker for jobs the 10 minute limit can divide.

limits.value: 400,000 GB-s a month is 3,200,000 instance-seconds at the minimum 128 MB allocation, which is 37.0 days of one always-resident 128 MB worker, so the grant is slightly larger than a month but a single function execution is capped at 10 minutes on the consumption plan and cannot stay resident.

evidence.proved: monthly free grant of 1 million executions and 400,000 GB-s per subscription, with the footnote that grants apply to paid consumption subscriptions only, quoted
Azure lists 65 or more always-free services that persist for as long as the account exists, separate from the 12-month list
the always-free table lists Functions at 1 million requests, distinct from the 12-month-only VM allowances

notes: The 400,000 GB-s figure is a memory-time budget, not a wall-clock one: the same 400,000 buys 37 days at 128 MB, 18.5 days at 256 MB, or 9.3 days at 512 MB. The 'paid consumption subscriptions only' footnote is the unresolved part, because it may exclude the free trial subscription a user would start with; a probe of the portal quota page on a fresh subscription would settle it.
